panel.name: {app} AI
panel.hint_focus_mac: Enter send · Tab mode · ⌃L clear · Esc back
panel.hint_focus: Enter send · Tab mode · Ctrl+L clear · Esc back
panel.placeholder: Ask anything — e.g. "find the 10 biggest files here"
panel.placeholder_approve: Enter to run · E edit · S skip · or type feedback

panel.intro: Tell me what you want to do in plain words. I'll suggest the commands (guide mode) or run them for you (auto mode, Tab to switch).
panel.intro_no_key: To start, add your {company} API key: click "Add API key" in the title bar, or open Settings ({keys}). Under Assistant you can also pick Claude, GPT or Gemini.

card.still_running: still running after {secs}s — handed back to {name}
card.busy: The terminal is busy with another program, so the command was not typed. Ask the user to finish or exit it first.
card.pane_taken: Since this command was judged, the user has taken the pane it was to go to (something runs there, or is typed at its prompt), so Flow didn't type it over what they're doing. Run it again to have it judged where it would go now.
card.folder_moved: Its pane's shell is in another folder now, so Flow judged the command again there.
card.folder_said: Its pane's shell has said which folder it's in, so Flow judged the command again there.
card.folder_unsteady: The shell of the pane this command was to run in kept saying it was in another folder, so Flow didn't type it: Flow judges a command in the folder it runs in.
card.pane_closed: The pane this command was to run in was closed while it waited, so Flow judged it again for where it would go now.
card.letters_as_keys: The command holds letters past ASCII, which the shell at this prompt may take as keys, not letters: bash's locale has just changed into one that isn't UTF-8, or Flow's hook doesn't run there (it isn't the shell Flow started, or bash's PROMPT_COMMAND is read-only). So the command was not typed. Where the locale has just changed, a command without such letters first (`true` will do) brings a prompt that takes them; else write them as bytes, $'\xc3\xbc' for ü.
card.elsewhere: Flow didn't open it: the path isn't on one of this computer's own drives, and a file on another computer is never opened for the assistant, since opening it could hand that computer your sign-in. To give it to the assistant, copy it to this computer first.
card.link_waits: waiting for you to finish in your browser for {server}

key_dialog.server_keys: Enter to keep · Ctrl+V to paste · Esc to cancel

key_dialog.keys_mac: Enter to save · ⌘V to paste · Esc to skip for now
key_dialog.keys: Enter to save · Ctrl+V to paste · Esc to skip for now

key_dialog.not_a_key_plain: That doesn't look like a {company} API key.

theme_font.label: Its font
theme_font.hint: The machine's own font. Off, Flow's, with the rest of the theme as it is.

theme_crt.label: Its tube
theme_crt.hint: The machine's screen, curved and scanned as a CRT. Off, flat glass.

theme_colors.label: Its colors
theme_colors.hint: The machine's own colors, programs' sixteen among them, chosen to read on its screen. Off, Flow's colors.

theme_frame.label: Its window frame
theme_frame.hint: The shell window's frame round each pane, as its desktop drew it: a title bar with the tab's name, three lines and depth gadgets that bring the window in front of the others and send it behind them, a sizing gadget in the corner, and an outline. Off, the text alone.

theme_sound.hint: One of the machine's sounds, while Sound's Machines is on.

cursor_speed.label: Cursor speed
cursor_speed.hint: How fast the cursor glides to where it goes: slower feels heavier, faster keeps up. Each theme sets its own, a teletype's heavier than a PC's. With Cursor glide off it still steps along as you type.

efficient.label: Efficient mode
efficient.hint: For real work: pauses the liquid, CRT, effects and theme sounds, and holds the turning logo still. Your settings come back when it's off.
efficient.hint_battery: On while the computer runs on battery (Efficient on battery). Switch it off and it stays off until it's plugged in or Flow quits.
efficient.hint_low_power_mac: On while the Mac is in Low Power Mode (Efficient on battery). Switch it off and it stays off until Low Power Mode ends or Flow quits.
efficient.hint_low_power: On while energy saver is on (Efficient on battery). Switch it off and it stays off until energy saver goes off or Flow quits.

efficient_on_battery.label: Efficient on battery
efficient_on_battery.hint_mac: Efficient mode comes on while the Mac is on battery or in Low Power Mode. Turned off then, it stays off until that ends or Flow quits.
efficient_on_battery.hint_windows: Efficient mode comes on while the computer is on battery or energy saver is on. Turned off then, it stays off until that ends or Flow quits.
efficient_on_battery.hint: Efficient mode comes on while the computer runs on battery. Turned off then, it stays off until it's plugged in or Flow quits.

settings.title: Settings
settings.keys: ↑↓ choose · ←→ change · Enter toggle · Esc close

search.none: No setting has “{query}” in its name, its words or its key in config.toml.
search.keys: Type to search · ↑↓ choose · ←→ change · Enter go to it · Esc clear

section.hint: Enter or a click shows or hides this section's settings; ← hides them and → shows them. A section stays as you leave it.

language.label: Language
language.hint: Flow's menus, settings and messages. Automatic follows your system's language. The assistant answers in it too.

theme.label: Theme
theme.hint: Flow's own look, one after an old machine (its colors, cursor and screen, and fonts of its time where you have them), or your own. An old machine, or your own, also starts new tabs with its start screen and gives their shells its prompt; your own keeps the colors, fonts and CRT you set, with a start screen, prompt and sounds you set below, which a preset file saves too. Themes you save under a name come last.

theme_real_numbers.label: Its real numbers
theme_real_numbers.hint: Shows this computer's own Ethernet address (with the host ID from it) and serial number in the start screen, in place of made-up ones, which otherwise stay the same on this computer. They identify it, so leave this off for pictures you share. On Linux the serial stays made up, since only root may read it.

theme_start.label: Start screen
theme_start.hint: New tabs start with the machine's start screen, typed out at the speed of its line.

theme_prompt.label: Machine's prompt
theme_prompt.hint: The shells in new tabs take the machine's prompt (READY., %, $) in place of your own.

own_start.label: Start screen
own_start.hint: New tabs start with it. ^ at a line's start centers the line; {version}, {os}, {chip}, {memory}, {mb}, {kb}, {bytes} and {shell} stand for what they say.

own_prompt.label: Prompt
own_prompt.hint: The shells in new tabs take it in place of their own: {cwd} is the folder, {n} the command's number, \n a new line. Empty keeps the shell's own.

own_baud.label: Typed at
own_baud.hint: How fast the start screen is typed out, in baud (bits a second, ten to a letter): a teletype's 300, a terminal's 1200 or 2400, or all at once.

own_sounds.label: Sounds
own_sounds.hint: What your machine sounds like, with Machines' sounds on under Sound: a tube's hum and its keys' clicks; a video terminal's sharper clicks and its beep; a tube with a disk drive seeking as it starts, with a fan or without; with a floppy drive seeking as it starts and as its disk goes in, and clicking while it's empty; with a chord as it starts; a sound chip's beep as it starts and its honk for the bell; with a printer printing a command's output; or a teletype clattering as it types, its bell near a line's end, its carriage at each return and its paper tape punch as output comes.

own_frame.label: Window frame
own_frame.hint: A shell window's frame round each pane wearing it, as the Flow notanAmiga CLI's desktop drew it: a title bar with the tab's name, three lines and depth gadgets that bring the window in front of the others and send it behind them, a sizing gadget in the corner, and an outline. It begins as the machine your theme began from had it.

saved_theme.label: Your themes
saved_theme.hint: Save as theme… keeps what's worn now under a name: the colors (programs' sixteen among them), fonts, cursor, glass, liquid and CRT, with a start screen, prompt and sounds where they're set. It comes after the built-in themes, under Theme and in the new-tab picker; a name used before is saved over. Chosen here, the rows above type its start screen and prompt, leaving your own as it is. Export… writes the one chosen as a theme package, a .tar.gz file that flowapp install puts among the themes on another computer, its fonts named but not carried. Delete removes the one chosen, leaving its colors, fonts and CRT on under your own theme. A preset file saved while one is worn moves it too.
saved_theme.export_title: Export the Theme as a Package

editing.keys_lines_mac: Enter new line · ⌘Enter done · ⌘V paste · Esc cancel
editing.keys_lines: Enter new line · Ctrl+Enter done · Ctrl+Shift+V paste · Esc cancel
editing.keys_line: Enter done · Ctrl+Shift+V paste · Esc cancel

screen_refresh.label: Screen refresh
screen_refresh.hint: How often Flow draws. Display keeps to your screen's rate; lower saves power. Unlimited doesn't wait for the screen: text shows sooner, at the most power.

on_top.label: Always on top
on_top.hint: Keeps Flow's window in front of every other window, as the title bar's on-top does, dropped down by the hotkey too. Off, other windows can come in front of it.
on_top.hint_none_here: Wayland lets no program keep its own window on top. Your desktop's window menu has Always on Top: right-click Flow's title bar.

tab_sidebar.label: Tab sidebar
tab_sidebar.hint: How the tab sidebar ({keys}, or the three lines left of the tabs) comes out. Pops out: over the terminal, leaving its size alone, until Esc, its key or a click outside it. Pinned: beside the terminal, which narrows for it, always out; its key moves the keys into it and out. In a window too narrow to leave the terminal 20 columns, it pops out instead.

tab_sidebar_width.label: Sidebar width
tab_sidebar_width.hint: How wide the pinned tab sidebar is, at most a third of the window. Dragging its right edge changes it too.

hotkey.label: Hotkey
hotkey.hint: A key that brings Flow forward from any app, and puts it away again while it's in front. Off takes none.
hotkey.hint_failed: Flow couldn't take this key: another app has it. Pick another.
hotkey.hint_failed_linux: Flow couldn't take this key. Wayland lets no program take a key for the whole desktop, nor an X11 one under it (XWayland); an X11 session does, where another program may have it.
hotkey.hint_none_here: Wayland lets no program take a key for the whole desktop, nor an X11 one under it (XWayland, which hears a key only while one of its windows has the keys), so Flow has no hotkey here. An X11 session has one.
hotkey.hint_press_mac: Press the key to be the hotkey, held with ⌃, ⌥ or ⌘ (an F key works alone). A key one of Flow's commands has is taken from it; the system's, such as ⌘Q, aren't taken. Esc keeps the one before.
hotkey.hint_press_windows: Press the key to be the hotkey, held with Ctrl, Alt or the Windows key (an F key works alone). A key one of Flow's commands has is taken from it. Esc keeps the one before.
hotkey.hint_press_linux: Press the key to be the hotkey, held with Ctrl, Alt or Super (an F key works alone). A key one of Flow's commands has is taken from it. Esc keeps the one before.
hotkey.hint_refused_mac: Flow can't take that key as the hotkey. Hold ⌃, ⌥ or ⌘ with a letter, a digit, `, Space or an F key, or press an F key alone. Esc keeps the one before.
hotkey.hint_refused_windows: Flow can't take that key as the hotkey. Hold Ctrl, Alt or the Windows key with a letter, a digit, `, Space or an F key, or press an F key alone. Esc keeps the one before.
hotkey.hint_refused_linux: Flow can't take that key as the hotkey. Hold Ctrl, Alt or Super with a letter, a digit, `, Space or an F key, or press an F key alone. Esc keeps the one before.

drop_down.label: Drop down
drop_down.hint_mac: The hotkey drops Flow's window over the top of the screen the pointer is on, in front and on every Space, and puts it away again (Always on top keeps it in front). Off, Flow comes forward where it was.
drop_down.hint: The hotkey drops Flow's window over the top of its screen, in front, and puts it away again (Always on top keeps it in front). Off, Flow comes forward where it was.

drop_down_height.label: Drop-down height
drop_down_height.hint: How much of the screen the window dropped down takes, from its top.

drop_down_slide.label: Slide
drop_down_slide.hint: The window slides down from above the screen, and back up as it's put away. Off, or in efficient mode, it shows and goes at once.
drop_down_slide.hint_linux: The window slides down from above the screen, and back up as it's put away. Off, or in efficient mode, it shows and goes at once, as it always does on Wayland, which lets no program move its window.

drop_down_hides.label: Put away when unfocused
drop_down_hides.hint: The window dropped down is put away once another app has the keys, as the hotkey would put it away. Off, it stays until the hotkey.

drop_down_over_full_screen.label: Over full-screen apps
drop_down_over_full_screen.hint: The window drops down over an app in full screen too, without leaving its Space. While it's down, Flow's Dock icon and menu bar go, and ⌘Tab passes it by; they come back as it's put away.

liquid_style.label: Liquid style
liquid_style.hint: Clouds of swirling ink, water with ripples and sunlight, thick oil with a rainbow sheen, or rain on the window. None is plain glass, with nothing moving.

water_view.label: Water view
water_view.hint: Above: looking down into the water. Below: underwater, with bubbles when you type.

sunlight.label: Sunlight
sunlight.hint: How bright the sun is: glints and caustics above, light shafts below.

electricity.label: Electricity
electricity.hint: Lightning flickering between the clouds. Higher strikes more often.
electricity.hint_rain: Lightning in the storm outside, lighting up the night, then its thunder: sooner and louder the nearer it strikes. It comes with heavy rain; higher strikes more often.

flow_speed.label: Flow speed
flow_speed.hint: How fast the liquid moves and swirls. Lower is calmer.

flow_amount.label: Flow amount
flow_amount.hint: How much the liquid stirs on its own when you're not moving the mouse.

rain_amount.label: Rain
rain_amount.hint: How hard it rains, from a drizzle to a downpour that runs down the glass in sheets. Drops also land where you type, and the mouse wipes them away.

ribbons.label: Light ribbons
ribbons.hint: Brightness of the light bands drifting across the glass.

palette.label: Palette
palette.hint_rain: Colors of the lights outside the window.

text_ripple.label: Text ripple
text_ripple.hint: How far terminal text rides the liquid, in pixels. 0 keeps text still.

opacity.label: Glass opacity
opacity.hint: Lower lets more of your desktop show through.

liquid.label: Liquid effect
liquid.hint: Off freezes the liquid where it is and stops its animation, which saves power. For no liquid at all, pick None above.

reactions.label: Reactions
reactions.hint: The glass answers the terminal: rings and splashes when a command ends, a tank while a program reports progress, the liquid leaning toward the assistant, and tabs that glow when a long command finishes behind them.

program_effects.label: Programs' effects
program_effects.hint: Programs can set off lightning, splashes, ripples and currents in the liquid where they draw (OSC 7731), as Flow Rogue's spells and blows do.

backdrop.label: Backdrop
backdrop.hint: The blur behind the window. Mica and Acrylic need Windows 11.
backdrop.hint_linux: The blur behind the window, where the desktop offers one, as KDE Plasma does. Elsewhere, as on GNOME, the glass is clear.

font.label: Font
font.hint: Terminal and panel typeface, from the monospaced fonts on this computer. Symbols it lacks come from other fonts.

font_size.label: Font size
font_size.hint: Terminal and panel text size, with what the window then holds and each character's size under it. {bigger} and {smaller} also work.

fit_screen.label: Fit window to
fit_screen.hint: Resizes the window, once, to hold this many characters at this text size: a terminal's, the PC's, a home computer's or your own.
fit_screen.hint_machine: Resizes the window, once, to hold this many characters at this text size, the {machine}'s screen first.

fit_text.label: Fit text to
fit_text.hint: Sets the text size, once, that fills the window as it is with this many characters, as near as whole points come.

text_color.label: Text color
text_color.hint: Terminal text that programs don't color themselves. Click the value, or press Enter, to pick any color.

phosphor.label: Phosphor
phosphor.hint: Everything in one color, as on a monochrome monitor: programs' colors, pictures, 3D models and Flow's own title bar and panels, each as bright as the monitor showed it, white the phosphor at full. Off is full color; the green and amber screens wear their own. Click the value, or press Enter, to pick any color.

cursor_color.label: Cursor color
cursor_color.hint: The cursor and its glow. Click the value, or press Enter, to pick any color.

background.label: Background
background.hint: The glass's tint behind the terminal, under any liquid; programs that ask are told it. Click the value, or press Enter, to pick any color.

startup_logo.label: Startup logo
startup_logo.hint: Each tab shows a logo beside Flow's version, the computer and the shell, as old workstations did, in the tab's own colors. Chip maker shows Intel's or AMD's for the computer's chip, and the Flow notaSun Workstation and Graphics workstation themes show their makers' own. From the next tab opened or restarted.

preset_file.label: Preset file
preset_file.hint: Saves the look to a JSON file: the liquid, glass, glow, CRT, colors, cursor and font. Loading one changes only what it sets, so it can hold just a few.

cursor_shape.label: Cursor shape
cursor_shape.hint: A block, an underline or a vertical bar. Programs can still change it while they run, as Vim does in insert mode, and go back to this one.

cursor_blink.label: Cursor blink
cursor_blink.hint: The cursor blinks while Flow is in front, and stays lit as you type. Programs can still ask for a steady or a blinking cursor.

cursor_glide.label: Cursor glide
cursor_glide.hint: The cursor glides along as you type. Off, it steps to each character at once and glides only further, such as to the next prompt. Without a GPU it always steps.

glow.label: Glow
glow.hint: How strongly the cursor, tabs, buttons and dialogs glow. A tab whose command finished behind it glows whatever this says.

crt_preset.label: Preset
crt_preset.hint: Ready-made looks to start from. Save as… below keeps your own under a name.

crt.label: Strength
crt.hint: How strongly the old-monitor look shows, over any liquid style. Off turns it off; the rows below tune each part.

scanlines.label: Scanlines
scanlines.hint: How dark every other line is. 50% is half brightness.

interlace.label: Interlace
interlace.hint: The lit and dim lines swap each frame, as on a tube. It draws every frame while Flow is in front, which uses more power.

phosphor_glow.label: Phosphor glow
phosphor_glow.hint: The light that bright text spreads over the lines.

phosphor_decay.label: Phosphor decay
phosphor_decay.hint: How long the phosphor glows after the picture changes, leaving a fading trace. Like Interlace, it draws every frame.

grille.label: Grille
grille.hint: The fine stripes of red, green and blue phosphor. A monochrome tube, under a Phosphor, has none.

vignette.label: Vignette
vignette.hint: Darker toward the corners, as at the edge of a tube.

curvature.label: Curvature
curvature.hint: How much the picture bulges, like a tube's glass. Clicks and selections follow the curve.

crt_saved.label: Your presets
crt_saved.hint: Save as… keeps the look above under a name, to pick from Preset; a name used before is replaced. Delete removes the one in use.

provider.label: Provider
provider.hint: Who answers: Anthropic's Claude, OpenAI's GPT or Google's Gemini. Each needs its own API key, and switching starts a new conversation.

model.label: Model
model.hint_anthropic: Opus is the most capable; Sonnet and Haiku answer faster and cost less.
model.hint_openai: Astra is the most capable; Sol balances speed and cost; Luna is the fastest and cheapest.
model.hint_gemini: Argon is the most capable; Flash and Flash-Lite answer faster and cost less.

effort.label: Effort
effort.hint: How hard the model thinks before answering. Higher is slower and costs more.
effort.hint_gemini: How hard the model thinks before answering. Higher is slower and costs more. Gemini's top level is high.

mode.label: Mode
mode.hint: Guide: you approve every step. Auto: the assistant runs commands; those it or Flow's rules find risky still ask. The rules are a check by pattern, not a sandbox.

web_search.label: Web search
web_search.hint: Let the assistant look things up online, such as install steps or docs.

memory.label: Memory
memory.hint: Keeps a journal of the assistant's tasks, and facts it's told to remember, on this computer, sent with each new conversation, and the messages you sent, which ↑ brings back after a restart. What looks like a password, a token or a key is left out.

memory_kept.label: Remembered
memory_kept.hint: Open shows the facts in your text editor, to change as you like. Clear, pressed twice, forgets the facts, the journal and the messages you sent.

instructions.label: Your instructions
instructions.hint: Your standing instructions to the assistant, in a text file of your own: sent with every conversation, followed where they don't get round Flow's approvals.

skills.label: Your skills
skills.hint: Playbooks the assistant reads when a task matches one, each a Markdown file in this folder, or kept by the assistant when you ask. Each has a switch below: one switched off isn't listed for the assistant.

skill_package.label: Skills from {name}
skill_package.hint: The skills that came with {name}: {skills}. Each is listed below with a switch, off until you turn it on, so installing an app never changes what the assistant reads; All on and All off turn them all at once. Flow's approvals stand over them as over your own.

mcp_enabled.label: Let outside apps connect
mcp_enabled.hint: Lets apps such as Claude Desktop, Claude Code or Cursor use Flow through flow-mcp, as far as you allow each: the first time one calls, a card asks what it may do. Off, Flow doesn't listen for them at all; nothing listens on the network either way.

mcp_connect.label: Connect an app
mcp_connect.hint: flow-mcp is at {path}, which an app's MCP config runs. Copy for Claude Code copies the command that adds it there; Copy JSON copies an mcpServers entry for Claude Desktop, Cursor and others.

mcp_app.hint: {app}, started by {path}. Forget, and it asks again the next time it calls.

mcp_kind.hint_read: Whether {app} may list your tabs and read what their panes show, and read Flow's help.
mcp_kind.hint_tabs: Whether {app} may open tabs and panes of its own, close those, and bring any pane forward. Your own tabs it never closes.
mcp_kind.hint_settings: Whether {app} may change what flow-settings may: the look, sound, the window. The assistant's settings and your themes stay closed.

mcp_commands.label: Run commands
mcp_commands.hint: Whether {app} may run commands, in panes of its own beside yours, never in your shells: not at all, asking you each time, or without asking. High-risk ones always ask.

ai_pane.label: Where it works
ai_pane.hint: Where the assistant's commands run: your pane while it's free (at its prompt, nothing typed), else a pane of its own beside it; or always one of its own.

helpers.label: Helpers
helpers.hint: Lets the assistant hand parts of a task to helpers, each in a pane of its own, working at the same time. Guide mode asks for each.

helper_model.label: Helpers' model
helper_model.hint: The model the helpers use: a smaller one costs less.

own.label: Working on its own
own.hint: Lets the assistant ask to work through a task on its own. Let it work, on its plan's card, runs its commands without asking, within the limits below, but for the few Flow's rules recognize by pattern as needing you.

own_minutes.label: Its time
own_minutes.hint: The longest a task on its own may take: twice what the assistant expects, and no more than this.

own_tokens.label: Its tokens
own_tokens.hint: The most tokens a task on its own may use. The Token cap still stops it.

token_cap.label: Token cap
token_cap.hint: The assistant stops before the next request once usage reaches this. Clear the usage or raise the cap to go on.

token_usage.label: Token usage
token_usage.hint: Since {date}: {input} in, {output} out, {reads} cache reads, {writes} cache writes, {requests} requests. Clear starts counting from zero.

api_key.label: API key
api_key.hint: Your {company} key is stored in the system credential store.
api_key.hint_none: No {company} key yet. Add one to use the assistant.

default_shell.label: Default shell
default_shell.hint: The shell for the first tab and new ones ({keys}). The + after the tabs opens any other.

reopen_tabs.label: Reopen tabs at start
reopen_tabs.hint: When Flow starts, the tabs open when it last quit come back, each with its shell, its theme and its folder. Restart always brings them back.

option_as_meta.label: Option as Meta
option_as_meta.hint: Option+key sends Esc+key for shell and editor shortcuts, instead of typing characters like ƒ and ©.

mouse_reporting.label: Mouse reporting
mouse_reporting.hint: Programs that ask for the mouse, such as games, editors and htop, get its clicks, drags and wheel. Hold Shift to select text over them.

click_moves_cursor.label: Click to move the cursor
click_moves_cursor.hint: A click on the line you're typing at the shell's prompt moves the cursor there, as the arrow keys would. Anywhere else a click selects as always.

scrollbar.label: Scrollbar
scrollbar.hint: A bar along each pane's right edge to jump through the scrollback: drag it, or click where to go. While scrolling it shows while you're scrolled back, the wheel turns or the pointer is at the edge, then fades.

keys_reset.label: All keys
keys_reset.hint: Puts every key back as Flow has it.

key.hint_add_mac: Press the key to add, held with ⌃, ⌥ or ⌘ (an F key works alone): the command takes it besides the keys it has. Esc keeps them as they are.
key.hint_add_windows: Press the key to add, held with Ctrl or Alt (an F key works alone): the command takes it besides the keys it has. Esc keeps them as they are.
key.hint_add_linux: Press the key to add, held with Ctrl or Alt (an F key works alone): the command takes it besides the keys it has. Esc keeps them as they are.
key.hint: Enter or Change, then press the key it's to be: Esc keeps it, Backspace leaves it none. Add Key gives a command another key besides. The keys inside Flow's own screens (Esc, Enter, the arrows) stay as they are.
key.hint_fixed: Quitting is the system's key on the Mac, the same in every app.
key.hint_press_mac: Press the key, held with ⌃, ⌥ or ⌘ (an F key works alone). Esc keeps the key it has, Backspace leaves it none.
key.hint_press_windows: Press the key, held with Ctrl or Alt (an F key works alone). Esc keeps the key it has, Backspace leaves it none.
key.hint_press_linux: Press the key, held with Ctrl or Alt (an F key works alone). Esc keeps the key it has, Backspace leaves it none.
key.hint_tabs: Press a digit from 1 to 9 held with the modifiers all nine are to take. Esc keeps them, Backspace leaves none.
key.hint_panes: Press an arrow held with the modifiers all four are to take. Esc keeps them, Backspace leaves none.
key.refused_typing_mac: That key would be typed: hold ⌃, ⌥ or ⌘ with it (an F key works alone).
key.refused_typing: That key would be typed: hold Ctrl or Alt with it (an F key works alone).
key.refused_help: F1 alone opens help for the screen in front: hold a modifier with it, or press another.
key.refused_system: That key is the system's, and never reaches Flow, or quits it: press another.
